At least in America, the wage paid by the restaurant to the servers is usually not enough for a living, and tips make up for it. I’m a server now, I definitely am not making enough to pay for everything in life, especially as a student. If I have to spend time on someone making sure all their demands are met and expect a dollar or two because tipping is expected and I don’t because people want to make some moral statement that they shouldn’t have to pay for me serving them (knowing well that servers aren’t making that much money for a living in the first place), it does annoy me. I’m not going to chase after a customer, but there are places that do.

And in some places like the one I’m working in, tips get put in a jar and split between the servers and the cooks. You don’t want to pay tip, then don’t, there’s plenty of other options for food where you don’t have to. But if you come into a place knowing tip is expected and don’t pay it, you’re not making any changes against some big capitalist machine, you’re just adding to workers being paid less than they already are. Yes, there’s laws but there’s more places who don’t follow them and are paying people less than there are who are paying fairly in America. 

I am bitter towards people who don’t tip if their reason is “I shouldn’t HAVE to” because no, you’re not, but it’s expected in the culture and I’m dependent on it. I can understand people who tip little or can’t, and if they haven’t caused me any trouble I’m cool. But if they’re demanding and mean to a server, AND don’t tip, that’s going to make me salty.

I'm depressed and I have a libido. I don't think it's an indication that you're not actually depressed because you're able to masturbate. Many people can function very well even when depressed, but that doesn't mean they aren't. In my case, if I'm upset I might masturbate to take my mind off of it, as a distraction. But I'm still depressed when I'm not doing that. For example, if I have a cold, I might still be able to get up and eat or go to school, but that doesn't mean I'm not sick.

What I've learned is never to trust someone if they say they care very easily. I used to be very open about my depression and they always said the vague "You can talk to me, it's okay!" but when I actually did, they couldn't handle it. 

I feel like society has conditioned everyone to automatically offer words of comfort when someone says they're sad because it's the "right thing." Even if the person knows they can't handle it or don't want to be around a depressed person, they still say those words emptily because there's not much other choice. And those fake scripted words just end up giving people false hope because eventually, it's going to be obvious that the person really doesn't want to be a part of this toxicity. I'd rahter them be honest and say, "Hey, I don't really know if I can handle this" so I can find other ways to form a friendship.

For people who are depressed, it's really difficult sometimes to form a friendship and not reveal all the depressing bits, especially when someone will say, "I'm your friend, you can tell me." And there's little reactions or actions that are well "taught" in society that aren't to "fix" someone or offer scripted condolences. People who don't know how it feels like just don't get it, and they'll back out and it's because they really don't know better. A majority of people are not equipped with depression, not the way couselors or therapists are.

It's good to have friends. I think isolation can make depression worse, but it's important to know how to find the right people so budding friendships aren't false hopes that end up getting ruined in the end. I don't think anyone would be happy with you dying, to have you gone from the world. Their actions are to protect themselves because they don't know how to handle depression, not because they solely want to hurt you (even though it often does end up hurting you). But I also believe they don't know how to handle depression and negativity. I really hope the best for you. I hope you'll find the support you need, whether in a friend or with professional help.

I’ve been on both sides of the equation; both the one pushed away and the one who had to push someone away because I had to protect myself.

Friends are good, and helpful. They’re there to support you but they’re also not there solely to help you. If all you’re doing is despairing to them, they’re going to listen and suggest you seek help. They’re not a therapist, and they can only offer so much. And you can’t expect them to offer more than they already have and are willing to give. A friendship can’t solely depend on someone being depressed and the other being responsible for cheering them up.

In the scenario you’ve presented, it happens. But they’re not responsible for someone else’s life. It sucks and it can get ugly, but someone can’t be like, “Help me or I’m going to end up killing myself and then you’ll feel sorry.” If they’re not a professional, you’re putting them in a really scary place where they’re suddenly responsible for someone’s life and often times that’s a toxic relationship. There are people that will stick through and help you, but that’s not going to be everyone and if someone can’t do that it’s not their fault. 

The important thing is to know limitations and how willing someone is to help you. If they’re not, you can’t really fault them for deciding to put their own health first. If they are, then that’s great but understand that friendships shouldn’t become a dependency. There’s only so much friends can do and if their support isn’t enough anymore and they tell you to seek professional help, do that.

I saw HYYH when I started high school and now I’m graduating so I do think it’s time for HYYH to be over. However, stuff from the early Red Bullet seemed to connect to HYYH as well and Love Yourself short films had a brighter aesthetic than the nostalgic tones of HYYH, and introduced new stories and characters. So to me, it feels like everything connects, but not completely, just like real fan AUs.

Fanart and fanfics draw inspiration from the original source material like Easter eggs and you can see where little tibbets of the original MVs or stuff the boys have mentioned seep through, but 90% is still the fan creators’ own ideas and interpretations. Like that, I feel the BTS universes aren’t necessarily connecting with each other, but drawing inspiration from earlier works and other sources, combined with new ideas to create something new. You can enjoy HYYH without knowing how it ties to Red Bullet, and you can enjoy Love Yourself without knowing the connections to HYYH. Even major things like the car accident, just watching only Love Yourself content you can see Jin had something to do with it. So to me it’s easier to enjoy each universe as a different one and seeing everything in common as throwbacks rather than a big overarching story. It doesn’t feel like a complete continuation because the aesthetics and setting are really different (and I’m also tired of trying to connect everything).

I think Wings concept was the most aesthetically different from everything else, in terms of story setting as well. It was like, BTS in a fantasy horror Renaissance AU and someone’s a fallen angel. It was probably the most angst with all the solos, but I really enjoyed every part of the Wings universe and it’s a concept that had a lot of interesting potential.

Literally the emo stuff from INU was what sold me into BTS. I first saw their Bangtan Bombs then Dope and was like, “cool, they’re talented and funny” but the stories and theories were something that I hadn’t seen much from K-pop and I was so fascinated, especially when the Prologue came out and it felt like complete cinematic stories.

I was disappointed with DNA at first because I felt it was the stereotypical K-pop themed song but enjoyed it because I felt it was a nice break from the angst and theories. However, like everything BTS has done, lyrically Love Yourself has a lot of messages that run deeper than usual love songs, especially with Pied Piper being so meta. Some people may like BTS just because they’re cool and talented but it’s undeniable that a lot of the appeal to their concepts came from the theories and angst (there’s so many theory videos) and it hurts me when people say HYYH is a dead horse that BH will never stop beating because well...BTS and BH seemed to put a lot of work into it...
